2.text: winner has the right to give the loser a stroke on the palm of his hand with

3.text: the stick used in the game, for every point he has gained on him. The game

4.text: is sometimes varied by throwing a bundle of sticks into the air and catching

5.text: them with the hand as they fall. The scoring and the ultimate reward are

6.text: identical with those of the hoop-game.

7.text: Gambling-games are little known among the Chukchee. I was told that

8.text: among the Maritime Chukchee on the Arctic shore there is a simple game

9.text: played for stakes, which consists in throwing a small piece of gristle against

10.text: a large flat stone so that it will rebound high in the air. The one who

11.text: catches the gristle gets the stakes, which are usually matches, copper caps,

13.text: At the present time many camps and villages have learned to play cards

14.text: from their Russian neighbors or from American whalers. Among the Reindeer

15.text: Chukchee of the Kolyma, passionate gamblers may now be met who have lost

16.text: their all in play against more clever Russian neighbors.

17.text: Children have various toys, most of them small imitations of objects of

18.text: every-day life, such as little boots, sledges, wooden or ivory dogs and reindeer

19.text: with the proper harness, snowshoes, bows and arrows. Grasping in each hand

20.text: a slender willow branch having many offshoots to represent antlers, the boys

21.text: will gallop up and down, playing reindeer.

22.text: Tops (Fig. 197, b) are favorite toys. Their shape is similar to that of

23.text: the American Eskimo top. Buzzes (Fig. 197, c) are made of various materials, —

24.text: ivory, wood, tough skin, and even a piece of dried fish. Much of the ivory

25.text: carving is also used by children for toys. An implement exactly like that

26.text: represented by Nelson¹ is used by the Chukchee as a kind of top. A specimen

27.text: of it was obtained on Anadyr Bay (Fig. 197, d). It consists of a horizontal

28.text: antler handle with one end broadened and containing a hole, through which

29.text: passes the rod of the top to be spun. This is kept from slipping out of the

30.text: handle by a knob at the upper end and a square piece of wood at the bottom.

31.text: The latter forms the body of the top. In spinning the top, a cord is wound

32.text: around the rod above where it passes through the handle and just under the

33.text: knob. By holding the top vertically and pulling the string off quickly, it will

34.text: spin rapidly for a short time with the knob resting on the handle.

37.text: The handle is bent slightly downwards. The hole and the knob are serrated,

38.text: so that in revolving the constant chafing produces a sort of buzzing noise.

39.text: The knob has four sides, with similar face designs on opposite sides. The

40.text: implement is used for a kind of game in which four persons take part, two
